generated_by: measured by hand against the running API on 2026-09-07, then frozen as tests/rag/test_retrieve.py::test_fusion_does_not_bury_a_translation_under_english_mass
finding: Textbook Reciprocal Rank Fusion silently destroyed cross-lingual retrieval on an English-heavy corpus.
query: Why did the CFO object to the payback period?
cause: RRF sums reciprocal ranks across both lists, assuming both retrievers could rank any document. A Hindi or Arabic chunk can never appear in a BM25 list for an English query because it shares no tokens, so it collected roughly half the fused score of any English chunk BM25 ranked for any reason.

before.fusion: sum of reciprocal ranks over both arms

unrelated_english_control.text: The marketing team prefers bright packaging for summer drinks.

before.consequence: the translations of the exact query ranked below a passage about summer drinks, and nothing failed

after.fusion: mean of reciprocal ranks over ELIGIBLE arms; a chunk sharing no query token is not BM25-eligible

principle: An arm that structurally cannot express an opinion about a document must not be counted as having voted against it.
verification: The regression test was confirmed to fail with textbook RRF restored ('a translation of the exact query fell out of the top 4: [en, en, en, en]') and pass with the fix.

per_embedder_after_fix.note: COUNSEL runs a different embedder locally and when deployed, so the fix is verified against both. Ranks are positions in a 16-chunk fused result for the same query.
per_embedder_after_fix.conclusion: MiniLM is measurably weaker for Hindi (rank 4 vs 1) but still places both translations well above the unrelated control, so it is usable for the deployed instance. The single-sentence margin in the A5 spike did NOT predict this difference — MiniLM's spike margin was the larger of the two.

how_this_was_nearly_missed: The regression test originally asserted a fixed top-N position, which passed on bge-m3 and failed on MiniLM. Because the CI machine has no Ollama, local runs tested bge-m3 and CI tested MiniLM, and neither tested the other. The test is now parametrised over both embedders and asserts the property that matters — a translation outranks an unrelated English passage — rather than a position that only measures how much English is in the fixture.
